A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Potentiometric nitrogen oxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The ceramic is gadolinium-doped ceria and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Al2O3 inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The bilayer structure improves the sinterability and moisture stability compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and P2O5 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Composite cathode comprising molybdenum disulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 800 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the molybdenum disulfide cathode. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the interfacial resistance is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A precursor of the LATP and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided.
