The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C.

assignee: Hwaseol Natl Research Inst of Energy Materials
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved high-voltage stability and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in anisole with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The sulfur is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising sulfur and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Mixed potential type hydrogen sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 400 degrees C. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 400 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the sodium beta-alumina sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
