title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A precursor of the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). With germanium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte powder with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method of handling the same in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte powder has a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of the sulfur is substituted by oxygen, the oxygen being enriched in a surface region having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm. The powder is prepared by mechanically milling Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower, heat-treating the milled mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in argon, and exposing the heat-treated powder to an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours so that the surface region is formed by controlled hydrolysis. The P-O bonds in the surface region are stable against water vapor, so that the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation measured in a sealed 1 L chamber after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less, and the ionic conductivity retention after the exposure is 85% or more. Because the surface region is thin and lithium-ion conductive, the grain boundary resistance of a pressed pellet remains 20% or less of the total resistance. The powder can be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box and is applicable to Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO-containing composite electrolytes.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte powder comprising a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of sulfur is substituted by oxygen, wherein the oxygen is enriched in a surface region of the powder having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm, and wherein a cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation of the powder measured in a sealed chamber of 1 L after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a silicon source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The sulfur is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LATP material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The resulting Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The resulting LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1.
