A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The roll pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The resulting Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: molybdenum disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises molybdenum disulfide impregnated in porous carbon and a carbon coating on the composite. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the molybdenum disulfide cathode. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, porous carbon, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The Li3YCl6 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. The LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell having a bilayer electrolyte of zirconia and ceria and method of producing the electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. The thin 5 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The stack shows stable operation over 200 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. The gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The stack of 200 cells can be paired with a lithium battery for load leveling. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising gadolinium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 5 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A precursor of the LLZO and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. With 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1.
