abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In the trigonal structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a gallium oxide with a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li7P3S11 material. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium bis(oxalato)borate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. With 2 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.2 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The content of LiI is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polycarbonate; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyacrylonitrile chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a titanium disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. The confinement of titanium disulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The active material titanium disulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. With zirconium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, zirconium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 2 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
