abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 100 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved interfacial resistance and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A precursor of the LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, 1,3-propane sultone, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The resulting Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll.
