The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The active material iron sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivering 1000 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium hexafluorophosphate as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and production method thereof
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the platinum sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The solid electrolyte of lanthanum fluoride conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The low electronic conductivity of the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1100 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LATP and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 300 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The electrode mixture of the solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LiF material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ErBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and graphene and lithium secondary battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. The active material nickel sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A lithium-sulfur battery with the nickel sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, graphene, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The resulting LiF and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. With 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. With 0.5 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl.
