A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: Provided is an oxygen-ion conducting ceramic electrolyte for a fuel cell that operates at 700 to 850 degrees C with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode. The gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode at 700 to 850 degrees C. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 700 to 850 degrees C operating range. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 700 to 850 degrees C. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium manganite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 88% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with gallium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The LLTO and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Composite cathode comprising nickel sulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The resulting LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li6PS5Cl material. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a lanthanum fluoride solid electrolyte for detecting hydrogen
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. The platinum electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 700 degrees C. The ceramic is lanthanum fluoride and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Amperometric ammonia sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia comprises a sodium beta-alumina ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The lanthanum strontium manganite electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The ammonia sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the lanthanum strontium manganite sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects ammonia.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; nickel sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
