The cathode delivering 1000 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 100 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid is described. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating on the lithium sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, carbon nanotubes, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LiPON layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The structure with the nickel-plated copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the content of LiI is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The resulting Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing 1,3-propane sultone as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a silver additive. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
