A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 50 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm.

title: Exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell and a sensing cell on a zirconia substrate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 400 degrees C. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The gold electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer ceramic sensor element comprising a ceramic layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia, an alumina layer with an embedded platinum heater, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and a porous protective layer, wherein the layers are co-fired.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which sulfur is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the sulfur cathode. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The sulfur cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.35 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and moisture stability of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sheet formability. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. With hafnium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute Of Energy Materials
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, LLTO, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm.
