Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The 1.2 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polycarbonate based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. With 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiPON layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The Li3PS4 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3YCl6. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1100 degrees C, and the resulting density is 97%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 89% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The warm isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a polyisobutylene binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a gadolinium-doped ceria solid electrolyte for detecting sulfur dioxide
abstract: Described is a thick film gas sensor whose sensing electrode is printed on a ceramic ion conductor. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor detects sulfur dioxide with high selectivity and a response time of 2 seconds. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The sensor with a response time of 2 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for sulfur dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects sulfur dioxide.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polycarbonate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LiF material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 75% or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, graphene, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The content of SiS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1.
