In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid is described. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The sulfur is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The confinement of sulfur in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The LATP and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7P3S11. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 4 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life and interfacial resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate at 1.5 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The composite shows a capacity of 1000 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode.
first_claim: 1.
