A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%.

title: Amperometric hydrogen sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 500 degrees C. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for hydrogen. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of hydrogen concentration at 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte of yttria-stabilized zirconia conducts ions between the sensing electrode and the reference electrode. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A lithium ion conducting glass may be used as the ceramic for a carbon dioxide sensor with a lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of hydrogen.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the grain boundary resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium manganite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The anode support contains nickel oxide and yttria-stabilized zirconia in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell. A 5 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell operates at 600 to 750 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The reversible cell with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 600 to 750 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 600 to 750 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium chloride framework. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In the monoclinic structure, indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a nickel sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Potentiometric oxygen sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: An amperometric sensor in which oxygen is pumped through a diffusion barrier by an oxide ion conducting ceramic is provided. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen. The sensor with a response time of 5 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for oxygen. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The limiting current is proportional to the oxygen concentration from 0.1% to 20%.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of oxygen.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which magnesium is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LLTO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 2 wt%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 30 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a molybdenum disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The 1.5 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating on the molybdenum disulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate and a film-forming additive
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The capacity retention of 85% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers.
