Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The LiF and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The resulting Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 0.4 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li3InCl6, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive vinylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria with a thickness of 8 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 700 to 850 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The anode support contains nickel oxide and gadolinium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. The cell may also be combined with a lithium battery in a hybrid power system operating at 700 to 850 degrees C. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the gadolinium-doped ceria cell. The solid electrolyte layer of gadolinium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 93% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY Co., Ltd.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of porous carbon to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The lithium sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. A separator coated with porous carbon traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C.
