The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. A precursor of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Potentiometric sulfur dioxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for sulfur dioxide. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting sulfur dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising sodium beta-alumina; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a niobium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 87% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 89% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and SiS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 94% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The resulting Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO material. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and porous carbon and lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The lithium sulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 2 mg/cm2. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Germanium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. In the monoclinic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Li2ZrO3 and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiF inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate.
