The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a titanium disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 85% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; titanium disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with LiF is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 85% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the titanium disulfide cathode. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which zirconium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; molybdenum disulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS (HNRIEM)
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The method prevents short circuit and improves the ionic conductivity without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and an ionic liquid as a plasticizer. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Potentiometric carbon dioxide sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The limiting current is proportional to the carbon dioxide concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The sensor operating at 300 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The ceramic is NASICON-type sodium zirconium phosphate and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 300 degrees C. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 300 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of carbon dioxide.

assignee: Qilunhe New Energy Technology CO., LTD.
title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 600 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The structure with the aluminum current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved electrochemical window and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A precursor of the LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, an ionic liquid, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, vinylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The capacity retention of 85% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. With 2 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the cycle life of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
