abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. With 1 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Al2O3 layer of 500 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a molybdenum disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into porous carbon at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode delivering 800 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LATP and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.3 to 0.75. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suppression of void formation improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. With 3 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The LLTO and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The uniaxial pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
