first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises molybdenum disulfide impregnated in graphene and a carbon coating on the composite. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The composite shows a capacity of 1000 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, graphene, and polyacrylic acid, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state battery. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the trigonal structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a molybdenum disulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. Polysulfide dissolution from the molybdenum disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 5 mg/cm2. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with graphene; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The capacity retention of 90% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium bis(oxalato)borate. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 2 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate is also described. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl acetate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The Li3PS4, LiF, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 5 nm to 300 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.
