title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. With 3 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The capacity retention of 92% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar aluminum current collectors. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 15%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The composite shows a capacity of 600 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising titanium disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite solid electrolyte with a lithium-rich surface composition matched to niobate-coated positive electrode active materials
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for use in a positive electrode mixture together with a coated positive electrode active material has an argyrodite crystal structure and a bulk composition represented by Li6PS5Cl, and a surface region having a thickness of 3 nm to 20 nm in which the lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio is 7.0 to 8.5, higher than the bulk ratio of 6.0, as determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The surface region, formed by treating the fired powder with lithium ethoxide in ethanol and drying at 150 degrees C to 200 degrees C, matches the lithium chemical potential of a lithium niobate coating layer on the active material so that lithium depletion at the coating interface and the resulting space-charge layer are suppressed. The solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, and a positive electrode mixture containing the solid electrolyte and niobate-coated LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 shows an interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V of 25 ohm cm2 or less, 40% lower than that of an untreated argyrodite. The surface region also lowers the hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air by 30% or more, and an all-solid-state battery using the mixture shows improved cycle life; Li10GeP2S12 type conductors can be treated in the same way.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a surface region in which a lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio is higher than a lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio of a bulk of the sulfide solid electrolyte.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= x <= 1.05.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium chloride ceramic ion conductor with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 3 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by uniaxial pressing
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 30 micrometers. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The capacitor rated at 35 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The capacitor rated at 35 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 35 V.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
