A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

assignee: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for nitrogen oxide with improved response time
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide comprises a lanthanum fluoride ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of barium carbonate makes the sensor selective to nitrogen oxide against interfering gases. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The multilayer structure with the lanthanum fluoride ceramic allows mass production by co-firing. The diffusion barrier is a porous ceramic with a pore size of 1 micrometer to 10 micrometers that limits the gas flux. A lithium carbonate auxiliary electrode may be used for detecting carbon dioxide at 400 degrees C. The sensor shows a response time of 5 seconds to a step change of nitrogen oxide concentration at 400 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting nitrogen oxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising lanthanum fluoride; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 400 degrees C.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 200 MPa. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 60 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyethylene oxide chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by atomic layer deposition followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing molybdenum disulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the molybdenum disulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous niobium anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a niobium solid electrolytic capacitor with a low equivalent series resistance and a high rated voltage. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 470 microfarad rating. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The 470 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter.
first_claim: 1. A multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor comprising a plurality of capacitor elements stacked and electrically connected in parallel, each capacitor element comprising a niobium anode body, a dielectric layer, and a conductive polymer layer, and a resin encapsulation, wherein the capacitor has a rated voltage of 16 V.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with tantalum and sintered with LiF is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a gallium oxide with a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The resulting LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 100 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 100 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 2 mA/cm2. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode.
