The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An all-solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a stainless steel foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which nickel sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. Polysulfide dissolution from the nickel sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the nickel sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The confinement of nickel sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising nickel sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: iron sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. A separator coated with carbon nanotubes traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Hafnium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte stable above 5.2 V
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 16:1.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet solid electrolyte doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 3 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 650 to 800 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of samarium-doped ceria conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. A hybrid system in which the fuel cell charges a lithium ion battery is also described. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising samarium-doped ceria, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 3 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an arsenic-free antimony source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is also described. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using polytetrafluoroethylene and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte oxygen sensor element with a heater and protective layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to oxygen against interfering gases. The sensor shows a response time of 5 seconds to a step change of oxygen concentration at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of oxygen.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate is also described. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. With 0.5 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. In the orthorhombic structure, erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state battery. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The 1.2 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 12:1.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The resulting Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
