A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 400 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, vinylene carbonate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising lithium sulfide, graphene, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the lithium sulfide is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

assignee: Industry-Academic Cooperation Foundation of Seodam National University
title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 300 mPa s to 15000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 35 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The 1.2 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. With 1 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive.

title: Composite cathode comprising sulfur and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfur cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The sulfur is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The cathode delivering 800 mAh/g is assembled into a lithium battery with a lithium metal foil. The confinement of sulfur in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 100 cycles. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; sulfur impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiBr at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a solid electrolyte is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained. The lithium hexafluorophosphate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The carbon nanotubes framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. With a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with carbon nanotubes by ball milling. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the molybdenum disulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The molybdenum disulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising molybdenum disulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 40 cycles or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LATP and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 1 wt%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Sulfur-carbon composite positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. The initial capacity of 600 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 600 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5 C. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 100 cycles is also described. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The carbon coating on the sulfur composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising sulfur and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described.
