A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The laminate of 8 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 50 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the lithium secondary battery. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. With 0.5 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The additive lithium bis(oxalato)borate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium bis(oxalato)borate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The confinement of iron sulfide in the porous carbon suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 50 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5 V and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

title: Potentiometric oxygen sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 700 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 700 degrees C. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for oxygen. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The oxygen sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 700 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 700 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of oxygen.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. With 0.5 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.2 M and adding fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate is also described. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 500 cycles. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising lithium difluorophosphate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyethylene oxide and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. A solid electrolyte sheet of 20 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing vinylene carbonate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.4 V is provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. With 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 0.5 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 4 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cold isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by fluoroethylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The current collector of aluminum is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The capacity retention of 88% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising 1,3-propane sultone, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A precursor of the LLTO and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1.
