abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The widened electrochemical window improves the electrochemical window of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, tin, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The LATP and LLTO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tantalum oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.15 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 60% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99% after 100 cycles. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The LiF, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The lithium battery is operated at 60 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= y/a <= 0.5.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a iron sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. Polysulfide dissolution from the iron sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by warm isostatic pressing. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The current collector is a aluminum foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 180 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 250 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 50 mPa s to 2500 mPa s, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7P3S11. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The resulting Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, LATP, and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 160 degrees C.
