first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of nitrogen oxide.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium yttrium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: iron sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 3 mg/cm2. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1200 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The iron sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising iron sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for hydrogen with improved response time
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the hydrogen concentration. The limiting current is proportional to the hydrogen concentration from 0.1% to 20%. The ceramic is yttria-stabilized zirconia and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor detects hydrogen with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to hydrogen against interfering gases. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting hydrogen, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising gold disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The GeS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a nickel-plated copper current collector is also provided. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polycarbonate matrix. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 30 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium bromide framework. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.3 V is provided. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The additive lithium difluorophosphate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without vinylene carbonate. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The additive vinylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by roll pressing. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The roll pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 90% with the electrolyte. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The nickel sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The nickel sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The initial capacity of 800 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The composite shows a capacity of 800 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising nickel sulfide, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the nickel sulfide is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The cold isostatic pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. With a binder content of 0.5 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a lithium sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The cathode may also be used with a solid electrolyte to form a solid-state lithium-sulfur cell. The positive electrode is used in a lithium secondary battery with a loading of 4 mg/cm2. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g and retains 80% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5 C. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The cathode with a loading of 4 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising porous carbon; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a aluminum current collector is also provided. The roll pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 100 micrometers or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. A solid electrolyte sheet of 100 micrometers is used as the separator. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a magnesium additive. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The suppression of void formation improves the cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing.
