The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the ceramic ion conductor powder with the silver additive in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. The membrane is assembled with a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode into a lithium battery. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. A lithium-sulfur battery with the lithium sulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The capacity retention after 200 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. A separator coated with ketjen black traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent. A lithium battery pack comprising 2 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises lithium sulfide impregnated in ketjen black and a carbon coating on the composite. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the lithium sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of lithium sulfide. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 2 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A core-shell particle for a positive electrode, comprising a core comprising lithium sulfide and a shell comprising a conductive carbon, wherein the particle has a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The Ag-C layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 50 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 2 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 2 cells and a case is also provided. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. Polysulfide dissolution from the lithium sulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 80%. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 32% or less.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The polymer matrix is polycarbonate and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 8:1. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The plasticizer an ionic liquid enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.16 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The laminate of 4 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 40 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. A solid electrolyte based on the polymer host is used without any ceramic component. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by nitrile butadiene rubber. The laminate is pressed by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiBr, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% after 100 cycles. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly.
