Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 40 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a niobium oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LLZO, LLTO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The tin substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 88% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 380 degrees C to 630 degrees C.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid is described. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyacrylic acid. The active material is coated with a thin lithium phosphosulfide ion conductor layer so that the cathode can be used in a solid-state cell. The lithium sulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The lithium sulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising ketjen black; lithium sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 100%.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The capacitor rated at 16 V may be used in a charging circuit for a lithium ion battery. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of niobium; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polyaniline doped with polystyrene sulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 15 milliohms or less.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. With a sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The active material sulfur is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The sulfur loading of 4 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, LiCl, and LiI at a molar ratio corresponding to the composition to obtain a precursor mixture; mechanically milling the precursor mixture; and firing the milled mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an inert gas atmosphere.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The content of P2O5 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The additive lithium difluorophosphate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state lithium battery using it. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyacrylic acid binder
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and polyacrylic acid is described. The composite shows a capacity of 1200 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The sulfur is melt-diffused into ketjen black at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. A lithium-sulfur battery with the sulfur cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The confinement of sulfur in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with ketjen black by ball milling. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing sulfur with ketjen black; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the sulfur into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a silicon source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 200 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 20 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
