The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyethylene oxide and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 20 micrometers or less.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Mixed potential type nitrogen oxide sensor and method of manufacturing the sensing electrode
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 400 degrees C. The sensor detects nitrogen oxide with high selectivity and a response time of 2 seconds. The sensor shows a response time of 2 seconds to a step change of nitrogen oxide concentration at 400 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the sodium beta-alumina ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects nitrogen oxide.

title: Electrolyte additive for forming a stable passivation film on a silicon negative electrode
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.5 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Potentiometric ammonia sensor having an auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of ammonia concentration at 400 degrees C. A porous protective layer of alumina covers the gold sensing electrode to prevent poisoning by particulates. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The gold electrode keeps a stable output over 1000 hours at 400 degrees C. The sensor detects ammonia with high selectivity and a response time of 20 seconds. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising gold, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of ammonia.

assignee: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a UV-crosslinked network of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The additive 1,3-propane sultone is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 60 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The cell charged to 4.5 V retains 85% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 1000 cycles is 85% with the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by vinylene carbonate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and vinylene carbonate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The binder content is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode slurry containing a sulfide active material and polyvinylidene fluoride binder
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery comprises nickel sulfide impregnated in porous carbon and a carbon coating on the composite. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the nickel sulfide cathode. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 80% at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyvinylidene fluoride in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing nickel sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the nickel sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, 1,3-propane sultone, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The cell charged to 4.4 V retains 92% of its capacity after 300 cycles. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The additive is decomposed to form a solid electrolyte interphase that is stable at 60 degrees C. The capacity retention of 92% after 300 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without 1,3-propane sultone. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Amperometric carbon dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of carbon dioxide concentration at 700 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The sensor with a response time of 20 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for carbon dioxide. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of carbon dioxide.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium battery is operated at 25 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The edge of the 100 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 2 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LiPON layer of 100 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The resulting LATP and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 40% or less, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 30 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by polytetrafluoroethylene.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 300 kPa or more.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARHC INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LDT.
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and method for producing the same
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers.

title: Solid state electrochemical sensor for hydrogen with improved response time
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid state electrochemical sensor element with a built-in heater that keeps the ceramic at 500 degrees C. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of hydrogen concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The hydrogen sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the gadolinium-doped ceria sensor in an exhaust gas.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising lithium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects hydrogen.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: sulfur positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which sulfur is confined in the pores of porous carbon to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. Polysulfide dissolution from the sulfur cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides. The composite shows a capacity of 1000 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The porous carbon framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of sulfur. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising sulfur, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the sulfur is 5 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LATP and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 300 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the moisture stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium iron phosphate electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
