A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 360 degrees C to 610 degrees C, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more.

title: Solid polymer electrolyte film with improved mechanical strength and ionic conductivity
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, succinonitrile, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 20:1.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The tin content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The plasticizer an ionic liquid is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

assignee: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector of copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 4 cells and a case is also provided. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 60 degrees C. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 60 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 100 mPa s to 5000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 180 degrees C.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by cold isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The cold isostatic pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, lithium difluorophosphate, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.0 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The 1.0 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. With 3 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 3 wt%.

assignee: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.48 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.8 V or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition for lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and a film-forming additive. The cell retains 92% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. The 1.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The lithium salt is lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium hexafluorophosphate in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding 1,3-propane sultone in an amount of 1 wt%.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the solid electrolyte layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The semi-interpenetrating network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 30 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a aluminum current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The roll pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 25 degrees C.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved dendrite suppression and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state lithium battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1.
