first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LiF material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 40 nm to 200 nm.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 600 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Disclosed is a semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte in which a crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile holds a lithium salt and provides dimensional stability. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 20:1. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.2 mS/cm. The titania nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyacrylonitrile. titania nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A lithium metal battery with the polymer electrolyte and a lithium foil of 50 micrometers is also provided. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium hexafluorophosphate, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 300 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A capacity retention of 90% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 45% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A precursor of the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous tantalum anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with p-toluenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The 220 microfarad capacitor smooths the output of a lithium battery converter. The solid electrolyte of the capacitor is formed from a conductive polymer dispersion. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 10 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The tantalum capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of tantalum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) doped with p-toluenesulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 10 milliohms or less.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium battery pack comprising 4 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 8 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The uniaxial pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 100 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The stable passivation film formed by 1,3-propane sultone suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.3 V. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The additive 1,3-propane sultone decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The additive 1,3-propane sultone forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 30 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-P2O5 glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the lithium secondary battery. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polycarbonate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The solid electrolyte membrane is a polymer that replaces the separator and the liquid electrolyte. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The membrane of 50 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate.
first_claim: 1. A composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether, and a photoinitiator, wherein a molar ratio of ethylene oxide units to lithium is 8:1.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium erbium bromide ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 2, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which titanium is substituted for part of the scandium in a lithium scandium chloride framework. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state battery. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF material. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 130 degrees C to 370 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.0 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by lithium bis(oxalato)borate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The 1.0 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. With 2 wt% of lithium bis(oxalato)borate, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The solid electrolyte interphase formed by the additive has a thickness of 10 nm to 50 nm and contains lithium fluoride and lithium carbonate. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium tetrafluoroborate in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.0 M and adding lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt%.

assignee: Hwaseol National Research Institute of Energy Materials
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3InCl6. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 0.5 wt%. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a non-aqueous electrolyte, comprising dissolving lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate to a concentration of 1.5 M and adding tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 0.5 wt%.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 100 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The 100 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane.
