The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The alumina nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a stainless steel current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and nitrile butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. A solid electrolyte sheet of 50 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 45 wt% to 90 wt%.

title: Zirconium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.12 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and production method thereof
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate and vinylene carbonate as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The additive vinylene carbonate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.5 M in a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, a mixed solvent of propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate, a first additive comprising vinylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and styrene-butadiene rubber are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 600 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the ionic conductivity in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solvent is ethyl propionate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The lithium salt is lithium perchlorate and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The lithium perchlorate salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium perchlorate; and a plasticizer comprising tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, porous carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride is described. The active material iron sulfide is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyvinylidene fluoride. The composite shows a capacity of 1000 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing iron sulfide with porous carbon; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the iron sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide, and a conductive agent.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: Described is a free-standing polymer electrolyte film of 20 micrometers thickness for a lithium battery. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the UV-crosslinked polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyethylene oxide; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising an ionic liquid in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

assignee: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar stainless steel current collectors. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Electrochemical gas sensor with a yttria-stabilized zirconia solid electrolyte for detecting carbon dioxide
abstract: Provided is a potentiometric sensor having an auxiliary electrode phase of lithium carbonate that converts the carbon dioxide concentration into an ionic activity. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The carbon dioxide sensor can be used for combustion control and emission monitoring at 500 degrees C. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 500 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor operating at 500 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide. A heater pattern of platinum is embedded in an alumina layer laminated to the ceramic to keep the sensor at 500 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting carbon dioxide, comprising: a ceramic body comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia; a sensing electrode comprising lanthanum strontium manganite disposed on a first surface of the ceramic body; a reference electrode disposed on a second surface of the ceramic body; and a heater that heats the ceramic body to 500 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The resulting LLTO, LATP, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The solid electrolyte provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the ionic conductivity are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Composite cathode comprising lithium sulfide and carbon nanotubes and lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium sulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and polyacrylic acid. The active material lithium sulfide is combined with carbon nanotubes and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the carbon nanotubes suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and polyacrylic acid in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. The positive electrode mixture may contain a solid electrolyte such as Li3PS4 as an ion-conducting additive.
first_claim: 1. A method of preparing a positive electrode active material, comprising: mixing lithium sulfide with carbon nanotubes; heating the mixture at 150 to 160 degrees C to diffuse the lithium sulfide into the carbon; and coating the composite with carbon by chemical vapor deposition.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a molybdenum disulfide cathode material for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of synthesizing it. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with graphene and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The molybdenum disulfide cathode material is inexpensive and environmentally benign. The cathode delivers an initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g and retains 90% of the capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. The molybdenum disulfide particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with graphene by ball milling.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising molybdenum disulfide, graphene, and polyvinylidene fluoride, wherein a loading of the molybdenum disulfide is 2 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The bipolar stacking of 4 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 600 kPa or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 16% or less.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte solution containing lithium difluorophosphate as an additive and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The capacity retention of 90% after 500 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without lithium difluorophosphate. The additive lithium difluorophosphate reduces gas generation during storage at 60 degrees C and improves safety. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and lithium difluorophosphate as an additive.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte containing a fluorinated carbonate solvent for a lithium battery charged to 4.5 V is provided. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.5 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.5 V. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 3 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.0 M and 1,3-propane sultone as an additive.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 200 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more during cycling is described. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium cobalt oxide, and a conductive agent. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 8 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium cobalt oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the ion-conductive solid layer is formed by the method of claim 1.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium yttrium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 200 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: A positive electrode with a sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 and a method of manufacturing the same are provided. A lithium-sulfur battery with the molybdenum disulfide cathode, a lithium metal negative electrode, and an ether electrolyte is also described. The sulfur loading of 5 mg/cm2 gives a high energy density of the lithium-sulfur battery.
